parsed.study_design: Comparative case study using policy/document analysis, field observations, and semi-structured interviews
parsed.population_and_sample: Residents of unplanned settlements and relevant utility, government, urban-development, and civil-society actors in Lima and Delhi; the fieldwork included 30 semi-structured interviews with sector professionals and more than 40 interviews with urban developers and civil-society members in each city.
parsed.exposure: Utility reforms, regulatory adjustments, documentation and tenure requirements, emergency legislation, community layout plans, informal addressing, and other institutional arrangements governing network extension in unplanned settlements.
parsed.outcome: Extension and coverage of household water and sanitation networks in Lima, including connection eligibility and infrastructure availability; electricity access in Delhi serves as the comparative case.
parsed.rationale: The “Case studies: contexts and method” section (pp. 94–95) identifies a comparative empirical design based on document and policy analysis, two six-month field investigations, observations, and interviews. The Lima findings report water and sanitation connection coverage and show how possession attestations, emergency legislation, utility programs, and layout plans enabled or constrained network extension in unplanned settlements (pp. 95–98).
